newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-IRELAND'S MCCOY IS REAL CHELTENHAM STAR.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-IRELAND'S MCCOY IS REAL CHELTENHAM STAR.

text.p: Ireland's Tony McCoy was the star performer on the first day of the Cheltenham Festival on Tuesday when he landed a double for the Martin Pipe stable, including a breath-taking success in the Champion Hurdle on Make A Stand.

McCoy, 22, opened his Festival account for 1997 when he guided Or Royal (11-2) to victory in the Grade One Arkle Challenge Chase and then followed up with a win aboard 7-1 chance Make A Stand in the Champion.
Make A Stand produced his hallmark display of front-running and fluent hurdling to win in a record time of three minutes 48.40 seconds, lowering the previous mark by one tenth of a second.
The County Antrim-born jockey has now ridden three Festival winners in his career.

"It is a great feeling on a horse to make all the running as he was there to be shot at but he kept going," McCoy said after his all-the-way win on Make A Stand. who has progressed brilliantly through the handicap ranks to the very top echelon.
"I rode the race to suit him and as if there was nothing else in the race. That's the way you have to do it. It is an unbelievable feeling. The feeling's good and I want some more," he added.
McCoy caused a surprise in January when he announced that he was joining forces with hard task-master Pipe, bringing to an end his association with rival trainer Paul Nicholls.
Some people in racing questioned the wisdom of the decision, but McCoy can hardly have got off to a better start to his career as Pipe's stable jockey.

"He did a terrific job," Pipe said after Make A Stand's $200,000 triumph in the Champion Hurdle. "I was very nervous as they made the top of the hill but Tony kept a little bit in hand and sprinted away going down the hill and kept going."
McCoy only began riding in Britain three years ago and Tuesday's feat rounds off a remarkably rapid rise to the top.
He was champion jockey for the first time last season and, barring injury, appears a certainty to retain his title at the end of the current campaign.
McCoy etched his name in British jump racing's record books in November when completing the fastest century of winners, beating the previous record by 30 days.
